rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP. CI. To erect a Scheame ... by Tables of REGIOMONTANUS
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: New printed Chapter CI (sequential editorial CII) demonstrates constructing a natal chart using Regiomontanus house tables.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Separate from accident-fitting Chapter C above the original printed divider.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The merchant's example gives birth Thursday 19 September 1616.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Historical Julian calendar, identity, and birth-time evidence not independently authenticated.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The merchant's corrected/reported time is specifically 2:24:25 PM.
rules.original_source_qualifications: A source number, not a modern certified civil birth clock.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The birthplace is represented at latitude/pole elevation 53°.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Place name and longitude are unspecified here.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: fit place of Sun to that houre
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly first adjusts the Sun's longitude to the stated natal time.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: allowing time in Ephemeris of Origanus 1 ho 7 min
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He mentions an adjustment of 1 hour 7 minutes related to Origanus's ephemeris and the location.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Historical reference correction to inspect against original ephemeris.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The source gives the Sun at Libra 6°37′ for the example.
At Libra 6°, Lilly gives right ascension 185°30′.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Source numeric reference, needs independent astronomical parity.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: At 7° Libra, source right ascension is 186°25′.
The RA difference between 7° and 6° Libra is 55 arcminutes.
For Sun at 6°37 Libra he interpolates an increment from 55′ per zodiac degree.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Linear interpolation across one ecliptic degree.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Computed increment 55×37/60≈33.92′, source reports 33′.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Source's truncation/rounding method matters (nearest minute would be 34′).

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He adds the printed 33′ to RA185°30′, producing source solar RA186°03′.
rules.original_source_qualifications: This differs by about one arcminute from nearest-minute rounding.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Source converts 2 hours of clock time into 30° equatorial motion.
Twenty-four time minutes contribute 6° equatorial arc.
The worked clock conversion refers to 30 seconds, although the original natal time is 25 seconds.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Five-second time discrepancy; arcminutes are rounded/truncated.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He adds the rounded time-angle components to 36°07′.
rules.original_source_qualifications: For exact natal time 2:24:25, correct angular increment is 36°06′15″; source uses coarser rounded 36°07′.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: RA Sun 186 03 plus time36 07 yields MC222 10
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The source obtains meridian/MC right ascension 222°10′.
He looks for corresponding ecliptic degree from RA table, finding 15° Scorpio at 222°31′.
He chooses the RA value for 14° Scorpio as lower bracket.
rules.original_source_qualifications: No leap from direct RA to ecliptic degree without lookup.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly uses values for 15° Scorpio and 14° Scorpio, differing 1° RA.
The 39 arcminutes toward the next degree place MC at Scorpio14°39′.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Printed interpolation corresponds to ecliptic arc minutes treated at unit slope in this row.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He fixes tenth-house cusp Scorpio14°39′.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Example outcome of source computation, not independently verified natal configuration.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: continual addition of thirty degrees to RA Midheaven
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: For subsequent house positions he adds 30° to the MC RA in equatorial longitude.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Uses Regiomontanus house-system construction; 12th, 11th, Asc, 2nd, 3rd at spaced equatorial arcs.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: enter Table oblique ascensions belonging to every house
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Translate those equatorial arcs via an oblique-ascension table for corresponding house pole.
He directs students to Regiomontanus p175 for the positions/elevations of intermediary house circles.
The geographic natal latitude is 53° for this example.
At latitude 53°, Lilly obtains 33°34′ as the house-pole value for 11th and 3rd.
He rounds 33°34′ to 34° to avoid interpolation and notes a small degree-level difference.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Approximate computational shortcut, not exact Regiomontanus geometry.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: At latitude 53°, the table gives ~48°59′ for twelfth and second houses.
He chooses 49° table as nearly equal to 48°59′.
The eleventh cusp's equatorial OA target is 252°10′.
The target for the eleventh-house cusp is 252°10′ using the 34° oblique-ascension grid.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Source calculation, not independent chart parity.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The eleventh cusp is at end of Scorpio, equivalently Sagittarius 0°.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Zodiac boundary equivalence; historic sign glyph checked.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The twelfth-house oblique ascension target is 282°10′ in the 49° pole table.
The 49° OA table brackets twelfth cusp with Sagittarius 14° and 15° values.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Original end points need independent source table parity.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The twelfth cusp interval between consecutive tabular degrees is 1°16′, or 76 arcminutes.
The desired target lies 61′ of OA above Sagittarius14°.
The source estimates 61/76 of zodiac degree as 49 zodiac arcminutes.
He records the twelfth cusp approximately Sagittarius14°49′.
The Ascendant OA target is 312°10′ under actual geographic latitude 53°.
The Ascendant is bracketed in the 53° OA table by Capricorn6° and 7°.
The table difference between these positions is 59′.
The desired OA is 39′ above Capricorn6°.
Zodiac interpolation gives about 39′ into the sixth degree, but the printed figure takes 37′.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Source p556 seems to say 37′ despite displayed 39:59 ratio; arithmetic requires ~39.7′. Preserve as possible numerical error.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The printed conclusion gives Ascendant Capricorn6°37′ rather than the ~6°40′ implied by the displayed table values 311°31′, 312°30′ and target312°10′.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Three-arcminute disagreement; could reflect illegible source value or earlier rounding, requires independent table image check.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly's final ascendant is Capricorn6°37′.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Use original output separately from corrected interpolation.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The 2nd cusp equatorial OA target becomes 342°10′.
He gives second cusp Aquarius23°30′.
Third-house target wraps 372°10′ to 12°10′.
Third cusp uses the same rounded 34° house-pole table as eleventh.
Final third-house cusp is Aries18°34′.
Cusp ten Scorpio14°39′ with RA222°10′.
Cusp eleven Scorpio30° or Sagittarius0°, OA252°10′.
Cusp twelve Sagittarius14°49′, OA282°10′.
Asc Capricorn6°37′, OA312°10′.
Second cusp Aquarius23°30′, OA342°10′.
Third cusp Aries18°34′, OA12°10′ modulo full circle.
Houses four through nine are implicitly obtained by zodiacal opposition to the six listed cusps.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Original example lists six; do not fabricate a separate printed second half.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: reduce diurnal motion Planets to time of Birth
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Planetary positions must be adjusted by diurnal motion to exact natal clock.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Ephemeris sampling at correct time and latitude necessary.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: add Part Fortune north south nodes
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He instructs including Part of Fortune and lunar nodes in the chart.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: allow motion required latitude and pole
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He calls for geographical/time adjustments before final planetary positions.
The original birth time is repeated explicitly as 2:24:25 PM.
He adds an ephemeris/London correction of about 1h07m and says use ~3h31m motion.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: birth place more east than London
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He says the birthplace lies east of London, motivating the offset.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Actual place name and longitude unresolved.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: slight discrepancy acceptable without sensible error
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He treats minute-level rounding in ephemeris motion as immaterial.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Authorial precision judgment, not validated astronomy parity.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Bredon Allen used alternative equating little
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He attributes a less-used alternate way of adjusting birth time to Bredon and Allen.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Historical practitioners, references not independently audited.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP. CII Of things considerable before judgement

rules.original_source_qualifications: This premise belongs to next chapter, not independently validated here.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: It introduces evaluating strengths/debilities of planets in houses and zodiac signs.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Belief system not an independent predictive result.
